pr_title: wayland_common: guard against negative configure sizes
pr_body:
Per xdg-shell protocol specification, it's not illegal for compositor to send negative width and height values. But negative values are nonsense to mpv, and can cause protocol error afterwards, like `xdg_surface::set_window_geometry` which doesn't accept negative values. Treat any negative values as zero (client determines size) for now.

Fixes https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/issues/13301.
pr_comments:
Download the artifacts for this pull request:

<details><summary>Windows</summary>

* [mpv-i686-w64-mingw32](https://nightly.link/mpv-player/mpv/actions/artifacts/1175850319.zip)
* [mpv-x86_64-w64-mingw32](https://nightly.link/mpv-player/mpv/actions/artifacts/1175850321.zip)
</details>

This is a compositor bug, clients shouldn't be expected to work around the compositor sending bad configure sizes. See: https://github.com/swaywm/sway/issues/7505 and https://github.com/swaywm/sway/issues/7815

> it's not illegal for compositor to send negative width and height values

This is also wrong, compositors can't send negative values.

> compositors can't send negative values.

The protocol [doesn't explicitly require](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/blob/main/stable/xdg-shell/xdg-shell.xml?ref_type=heads#L1101) the configure sizes to be negative. `xdg_surface::set_window_geometry` on the other hand explicitly requires sized to be greater than zero. The absence of explicit requirement on the compositor side (which is the case for most of the wayland protocols) strongly suggests that the compositor may send negative values.

> This is a compositor bug

Whether Sway or any particular compositor considers this a bug is irrelevant. This is technically allowed by the protocol, which mpv conforms to. The proper fix is to revise the protocol so that the compositor can't send negative values, but as the current letters stand, clients need to handle negative values.

> The protocol [doesn't explicitly require](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/blob/main/stable/xdg-shell/xdg-shell.xml?ref_type=heads#L1101) the configure sizes to be negative

Yes, it's not explicit about it when it probably should be. However, we're meant to use these values as hints for our window geometry which explicitly specifies that it can't be negative. The protocol is broken if compositor can request us to set a value that it isn't allowed to accept. A PR adding text to make it illegal will probably be accepted, given past discussion around it in the wayland IRC.

Working around it is fine I suppose, but the commit message needs to properly reflect reality.

> Working around it is fine I suppose, but the commit message needs to properly reflect reality.

I think commit message is clear. And there is no workaround, it is simple input values sanitation as mpv downstream doesn't expect negative values.

> I think commit message is clear.

I am talking about the `Per xdg-shell protocol specification, it's not illegal for compositor to send negative width and height values.` part of the message. It *is* illegal for all intents and purposes, even if it isn't explicitly specified.

> it is simple input values sanitation as mpv downstream doesn't expect negative values.

But it is the same downstream that is sending us these negative values. Either it can't send us a negative value, or it has to accept negative values. Given that it explicitly specifies that it won't accept negative values, that means it is implicit that it also can't send us a negative value. The fact that sway does when turning on outputs is a compositor bug and illegal.

Related: https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/issues/6773#issuecomment-1465247360

From \#wayland:

```
2023-03-12 22:21:17	kchibisov	I'd assume compositor must not send negative configure values for xdg_toplevel?
2023-03-12 22:22:01	emersion	yea
2023-03-12 22:22:16	kchibisov	Got [3923471.427] xdg_toplevel@30.configure(-4, -27, array[16]) from sway.
2023-03-12 22:23:25	emersion	sounds like a bug
2023-03-12 22:24:11	kchibisov	I'll redirect the user then.
```

> However, we're meant to use these values as hints for our window geometry which explicitly specifies that it can't be negative.

The protocol says that the client should interpret the values according to the state:

>The states listed in the event specify how the width/height arguments should be interpreted, and possibly how it should be drawn.

For example, a compositor may send the `suspended` state, expecting clients to only treat it as a hint to not repaint while providing some dummy negative sizes.

> From #wayland:

That should not be considered an official statement until he creates a merge request in wayland-protocols.
Revised the commit message. Notwithstanding the protocol requirements, it's still a good general practice to sanitize values.

> For example, a compositor may send the suspended state, expecting clients to only treat it as a hint to not repaint while providing some dummy negative sizes.

Once again, height and width simply cannot be negative. This shouldn't even be a thing that needs to be mentioned, heck you have properties like "physical_height" and "physical_width" that don't explicitly state that they're guaranteed to be non-negative. It's common sense that logical sizes are non-negative.

> That should not be considered an official statement until he creates a merge request in wayland-protocols.

Some things are obvious and don't need to be explicitly stated assuming a good faith reading on the developer's part.

> This shouldn't even be a thing that needs to be mentioned

See the message in [xdg-shell: Clarify what a toplevel by default includes](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/222), and replace "decoration" with "negative size". Clarification is needed even if things may seem obvious.

issue_context.title: wayland/sway: mpv sometimes crashes with “Tried to set invalid xdg-surface geometry” when display is turned off
issue_context.body:
### Important Information

Provide following Information:
- mpv version: 0.37.0
- Linux Distribution and Version: Gentoo Linux
- Source of the mpv binary: compiled from repository
- If known which version of mpv introduced the problem: 0.35.0 worked, so some later (could it be related to 9e9abb1a0f6e2b6b9619bc5f6443a75bf89ee0c7?)
- Window Manager and version: sway 1.8.1, wlroots 0.16.2

### Reproduction steps

Play a video, pause, go idle till the display is turned off (or call `output * power off` via `swaymsg`).

mpv doesn’t crash every single time. But when it does, all running mpv processes crash.

### Expected behavior

To stay running.

### Actual behavior

```
[vo/gpu/wayland] Error occurred on the display fd
Exiting... (Quit)
```

review_comments: We should print a warning message if we receive a negative width or height instead of silently deciding our own window dimension.
